text:
john.cust: Hey team — production private VPC app started getting TLS handshake hangs right after tonight's scheduled cert renewal. Some requests 502/504 from our side. Anyone seeing this?

cynthia.support: saw the alert, can you paste a curl/openssl output?

john.cust: here: `openssl s_client -connect api.prod.internal:443 -servername api.prod.internal -showcerts` shows only the leaf cert — chain length 1. curl errors: 'Empty reply from server' intermittently.

kevin.oncall: checking rotator logs now. Do you use the private rotator bundle upload or the UI?

john.cust: rotator agent (our private bundle via S3). We didn't change config, just the scheduled renewal ran and the agent pushed new fullchain.

mira.eng-runtime: quick note — our rotator can reorder certs if the bundle has CRLF/newline anomalies or extra cert comments; LB (haproxy) sometimes trims perceived duplicate CA certs on reload.

john.cust: hmm we did get a warning about an extra newline in the uploader output earlier in CI but ignored it.

cynthia.support: can you run `openssl s_client -connect api.prod.internal:443 -servername api.prod.internal -showcerts -status` and paste stapling section?

john.cust: stapling says: no response received. Also our legacy Java clients (8u341) start failing while modern browsers work.

kevin.oncall: interesting — two hypotheses: 1) the server is sending an incomplete chain (rotator/bundle order issue), or 2) AIA fetch for intermediate is blocked by your firewall so clients that attempt to download missing intermediate fail (browsers do fallback differently).

mira.eng-runtime: looking at rotator upload metadata — the bundle included both an RSA intermediate and a cross-signed ECDSA intermediate. On our HAProxy side, we saw a reload log: `skipping duplicate issuer cert` and then `sent 1 certs to client`. That matches openssl output.

cynthia.support: reproduce steps we've asked customer to try: 1) replace LB cert with the previous (known-good) fullchain to restore traffic, 2) on a test host, add the intermediate manually to /etc/ssl/certs and test openssl client behavior, 3) allow outbound to issuer AIA URL temporarily.

john.cust: did 1) and traffic returned to normal. We don't want that as a long-term workaround.

mira.eng-runtime: root cause seems to be the rotator producing a bundle where the preferred intermediate ordering caused haproxy to dedupe and drop one cert (the cross-signed intermediate). Some legacy clients rely on the dropped intermediate instead of AIA fetch.

kevin.oncall: mitigation we pushed to rotator: add a post-upload normalization that forces fullchain order: leaf -> intermediate (issuing) -> cross-signed (if present) -> root(optional), and strip blank lines/comments before upload. Please update agent to v1.12.3.

cynthia.support: sent an email to customer with repro steps and timeline. Also advised to whitelist issuer AIA endpoints for egress and to pre-seed the intermediate in their internal truststore while they upgrade.

john.cust: appreciated. Any ETA on rotator fix?

mira.eng-runtime: hotfix merged and deployed to rotator service, agent v1.12.3 release notes: `fix: normalize bundle ordering and remove stray newlines to avoid LB dedupe`. We'll coordinate a scheduled agent update.

ops-bot: deploy 2380012500 by mira.eng-runtime succeeded in rotator-canary (sha: a1b2c3d).

kevin.oncall: follow-up items: - Support to validate uploaded bundle contents automatically and reject if ordering ambiguous - Add a diagnostic in console to show the certs haproxy actually loaded (from workers) - Recommend customers enable append_intermediate toggle in private configs if they have legacy clients.

cynthia.support: closing the urgent escalation for now since customer restored traffic with rollback; keeping thread open for follow-up until agent update rolled out. :thumbsup:
